prompt:
You are a senior information designer and editorial typographer who sets data tables for high-quality publications (statistical yearbooks, reference works, financial reports, technical documentation) in many writing systems, including Chinese. You judge by looking at the real rendered result.

Judge a table layout on all of these levels, in this order of necessity but as one whole:
1. correctness — every character visible, structure intact, nothing clipped or overlapping;
2. readability — natural line breaks, words/numbers/identifiers/semantic units kept whole, continuous reading;
3. function — easy to look up, compare, locate and understand the information for this table's real reading tasks;
4. visual order — alignment, grouping, hierarchy, consistent scale for elements with the same role;
5. visual rhythm — proportion, density changes, distribution of white space, spatial relationships;
6. overall aesthetics — balance, restraint, naturalness, harmony.
Do not assume that equal widths, symmetry, minimum height, the fewest lines, the golden ratio or any fixed proportion is good in itself; decide from this table's function, content and reading task, and look for counter-examples to your own rules.

Table: Prototype Controller Board BOM (language en).
Grid: 5 columns × 8 rows. Row headers: none declared.
Measured content facts (text px at 15px font, padding excluded):
  col 1: header "Part number" · longest unbreakable unit 165px · widest one-line content 165px
  col 2: header "Description" · longest unbreakable unit 107px · widest one-line content 526px
  col 3: header "Qty" · longest unbreakable unit 26px · widest one-line content 26px
  col 4: header "Unit price" · longest unbreakable unit 59px · widest one-line content 70px
  col 5: header "Supplier" · longest unbreakable unit 133px · widest one-line content 133px
Each column adds 21px of padding+border to its text width.
Viewport: 360px wide (dashed pink box in the renders). At 360px some words cannot fit unsplit. Horizontal scrolling is ALLOWED: the table may be wider than 360px (column widths summing to more than 359px) (the reader scrolls), or you may fit within 359px and accept the consequences. Fitting and scrolling layouts are judged as two separate classes; propose good layouts of BOTH kinds.
Rendering convention: a full render shows the WHOLE table; anything right of the dashed box is not clipped — it is reached by scrolling. Where a layout scrolls, an extra "viewport view" image shows only what is visible at first sight.
Fixed: content, font, 15px font size, padding, borders, colours, alignment. Only the column widths are designed; row heights follow from them.

Your understanding: {"purpose":"List the components needed to build a prototype controller board and provide purchasing details.","tasks":["Identify a component by part number or description.","Read the required quantity and unit price.","Find the supplier and compare purchasing details across rows."],"relations":["Each row connects one part number and its technical description to a quantity, unit price and supplier.","Technical values and package codes in a description qualify that row's component.","Unit prices apply per component; quantities are counts, not prices or totals."],"roles":["The header row labels five fields with distinct lookup and purchasing roles.","Part numbers act as identifiers even though no row-header column is declared.","Descriptions distinguish components and their specifications; quantity and price are compact numeric fields; supplier names identify sources.","The seven body rows are individual items with no declared groups or subtotal rows."],"keep_whole":["Part numbers, package codes, supplier names and numerical values with their units where possible.","Currency amounts and quantities.","Technical identifiers such as ARM Cortex-M3 and specification units such as 10 kΩ, 72 MHz and 2.54 mm where space permits."],"may_wrap":["Descriptions can wrap between phrases and specification items.","Multiword headers and supplier names can wrap at word boundaries when needed."],"same_scale":["Quantity and unit price should remain compact relative to the descriptive fields.","Part number and supplier need enough width for their identifiers; description benefits from substantially more flexible space."],"h_vs_v":"At 360px, fitting all five columns forces breaks within some identifiers and supplier names and produces tall rows. Scrolling can preserve those units and give descriptions natural line breaks, at the cost of moving horizontally between identification and purchasing fields."}

Image 1 is the one-line content overview. Then real browser renders of: d3r4A (full view, then viewport view), d3r4B (full view, then viewport view), d3r4C, d3r1C (full view, then viewport view), d3r0A.
Measured facts:
d3r4A: column widths [186, 210, 47, 91, 154] px · table 689×570 px · row heights [36, 60, 60, 106, 83, 60, 83, 83] · column headers on >1 line: 0/5 · tallest cell 4 lines · measured breaks inside a word: 0 · WIDER than the viewport by 329 px (horizontal scrolling)
d3r4B: column widths [186, 320, 47, 91, 154] px · table 799×454 px · row heights [36, 60, 60, 60, 60, 60, 60, 60] · column headers on >1 line: 0/5 · tallest cell 2 lines · measured breaks inside a word: 0 · WIDER than the viewport by 439 px (horizontal scrolling)
d3r4C: column widths [82, 96, 47, 91, 43] px · table 360×1407 px · row heights [106, 153, 176, 222, 199, 176, 176, 199] · column headers on >1 line: 3/5 · tallest cell 9 lines · measured breaks inside a word: 44 · fits the 360 px viewport (no scrolling)
d3r1C: column widths [186, 240, 47, 91, 154] px · table 719×477 px · row heights [36, 60, 60, 83, 60, 60, 60, 60] · column headers on >1 line: 0/5 · tallest cell 3 lines · measured breaks inside a word: 0 · WIDER than the viewport by 359 px (horizontal scrolling)
d3r0A: column widths [80, 100, 47, 69, 63] px · table 360×1244 px · row heights [60, 153, 153, 199, 176, 153, 153, 199] · column headers on >1 line: 4/5 · tallest cell 8 lines · measured breaks inside a word: 27 · fits the 360 px viewport (no scrolling)

Look at each render as a whole and in detail. For each design: what works, what is visually wrong, and the cause (which width). Then either propose up to 3 improved designs (refine the most promising, fix what you saw, or try an important unexplored idea) or, if further changes would not bring a meaningful improvement, set "done": true. Do not resubmit near-identical widths.
Reply ONLY JSON: {"critique":[{"design":"name","good":"","problems":"","cause":""}],"best":["your best design name(s) so far"],"done":false,"designs":[{"widths":[int px],"change":"what and why"}]}
